newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends firmer on dollar unwinding.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends firmer on dollar unwinding.

text.p: The won closed firmer against the dollar on Friday as traders unwound dollar positions in the belief the U.S. unit was overbought, dealers said.
"Market players, under heavy dollar positions, began testing whether the central bank would allow the dollar to fall below 890," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers said in the absence of central bank intervention dollar sales continued throughout the day.
The won closed at 888.60 against Thursday's closing of 890.60. It opened at 890.20 and moved between 888.30 and 890.50.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 889.70 on Monday, compared with 890.90 today.
The foreign bank dealer forecast the dollar would test the 885.00 level on Monday unless the central bank steps in to cap the won's rise.
"Traders will closely watch where the central bank intervenes," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said the government would be interested in depreciating the local currency to prop up exports.
